Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live"

IS: 9650-1980 




Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
HOOK, JOSEPH'S PATTERN 



( Reaffirmed 1998) 



1. Scope — Dimensional and other requirements for Joseph's pattern hook used in plastic surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

♦S: 9650-1980 

2.1 The tolerance shall be ± 0*1 mm for the dimensions up to 10 mm and it shall be ± V-0 mm for 
higher dimensions. 

3. Material — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 30Cr 13 of IS : 6603 - 1972 'Specification 
for stainless steel bars and flats 4 . 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The hook shall be free from pits, burrs, cracks, scales and other surface defects. 

4.2 The pronged end of hook shall be sharp. 

4.3 The hook shall be polished bright and passivated. 

5. Heat Treatment — The hook shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 430 to 
480 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Flexibility — Hold the hook in a suitable vice so that the hook portion protrudes outside the vice 
in the downward direction. Apply a force of 50 N at each hook portion and hold it for five minutes. 
After the test, the hook shall show no sign of damage or permanent set. 

6.2 Corrosion Resistance — Test the hook in accordance with IS : 7531 - 1975 'Method for boiling 
and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments'. There shall be no 
sign of corrosion after the test. 

7. Marking — Each hook shall be clearly and indelibly marked on the handle with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; 

b) The word 'Stainless Steel' or letters 'SS'; and 

c) Size. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — The hooks shall be individually packed in a suitable manner so that they do not shake 
much in the pack and the tip of the hook shall not come in contact with any hard surface resulting in 
any damage to it. 



Printed at Printrade, New Delhi, India
